findings.title: Hard-coded cryptographic value
findings.reasoning: Line188 initializes salt storage. Line193 read_exact(&mut salt)? must fill the entire salt from the decoded export or return before line210 derives a key. The zero initializer has no successful path to the KDF without replacement. Encryption independently fills a fresh salt with rng.fill_bytes at163 before its KDF at165.
findings.conclusion: No hard-coded salt use is demonstrated by this initializer. This is a control-flow review of the flagged salt, not a general cryptographic qualification.

findings.title: Access of invalid pointer
reasoning: GetSecurityInfo requests OWNER and DACL, requires ERROR_SUCCESS and non-null descriptor/owner/dacl at253-276.
The returned descriptor allocation remains live through the entire synchronous DACL inspection; LocalFree occurs at282 after inspection, not before.
IsValidAcl succeeds and GetAclInformation(AclSizeInformation) supplies AclBytesInUse before enumeration at289-309.
Each GetAce must return success and a non-null pointer at327-332.
ace_span_fits_acl validates the requested header span at333-340; its checked_add arithmetic rejects overflow, pointers before the first ACE, and spans beyond bytes in use at384-402.
ptr::read_unaligned copies a value without creating a misaligned Rust reference.
findings.conclusion: Under the documented successful Win32 allocation/out-parameter contracts and inspected call sites, this flagged read has validity, range, alignment and lifetime guards. No concrete invalid-pointer path was found; SARIF's actual modeled flow still must be matched.

findings.title: Access of invalid pointer
reasoning: This file is included only under #[cfg(test)] at private_state_windows.rs:725-727.
Both callers at191-192 and217-218 invoke read_only_descriptor inside with_private_security.

The constructor's CurrentUser, Vec<u32> ACL backing storage and stack descriptor stay alive until create(&attributes) returns; InitializeAcl/AddAccessAllowedAceEx and descriptor construction all check success.
GetSecurityDescriptorDacl requires success/present/non-null; GetAce requires success/non-null at43-72.
IsValidAcl, GetAclInformation and the checked header span guard all succeed before the flagged read at76-108.
The subsequent allow-ACE/SID-minimum/full-span checks at109-126 also bound the Mask write at130-132; it uses write_unaligned and only modifies this new fixture descriptor.
findings.conclusion: The fixture has a concrete allocation owner and bounded checked pointer read, not just a null check. No unsafe path at the flagged read was found under the documented Win32 contracts; this does not constitute a native Windows test run.
